rule.title: Disable Windows Event Logging Via Registry
rule.author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: Un proceso escribió DWORD 0 en el valor Enabled de un canal de registro de eventos de Windows (WINEVT\Channels). Esto desactiva ese canal y deja de registrar sus eventos.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos registry_set (Sysmon EventID 13) donde TargetObject contiene \Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WINEVT\Channels\, termina en \Enabled y Details es 'DWORD (0x00000000)'. Se excluyen wevtutil.exe, TiWorker.exe de WinSxS, TrustedInstaller.exe con Compat-Appraiser, svchost.exe en ciertos canales conocidos y procesos con Image vacío.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante puede apagar canales como Windows Defender/Operational, PowerShell/Operational o Sysmon/Operational para operar sin dejar rastro. Corresponde a la técnica ATT&CK T1685.001: debilitar las defensas desactivando el registro de eventos de Windows.
triage_steps: Identifique el canal afectado en TargetObject y su valor de seguridad: Defender, PowerShell, Sysmon, Security o TaskScheduler son de alta prioridad.
Revise Image, ProcessId y User del evento. Pregúntese si reg.exe, powershell.exe o un binario desconocido tiene alguna razón legítima para modificar canales.
Busque el evento de creación de proceso correspondiente y analice la CommandLine y el ParentImage de esa cadena.
Revise el mismo host +/- 15 minutos: otros cambios en WINEVT\Channels, ejecución de wevtutil cl, paro de servicios o cambios en la configuración de Defender.
Verifique si el canal sigue desactivado (wevtutil gl <canal>) y si hay una brecha de eventos desde la hora del cambio.
Busque alertas anteriores del mismo usuario y host, y verifique si el usuario hizo inicios de sesión remotos recientes.
Confirme con el equipo de TI si existe un ticket de cambio o una tarea de troubleshooting que justifique el cambio.
false_positives: Administradores que desactivan un canal específico, muy ruidoso o de diagnóstico, durante un troubleshooting documentado.
Instaladores o herramientas de gestión de configuración que ajustan canales de registro mediante el registro y no con wevtutil.
Actualizaciones de Windows que usan procesos que los filtros de la regla no cubren.
response_steps: Valide con el dueño del host o el usuario si el cambio está autorizado antes de actuar.
Si no está autorizado, aísle el endpoint y preserve evidencia: export del registro, logs restantes y la memoria del proceso responsable.
Vuelva a habilitar el canal (Enabled = 1 o wevtutil sl <canal> /e:true) y confirme que se reanuda el registro.
Investigue la actividad ocurrida durante la brecha de logs usando EDR, telemetría de red y logs centralizados.
Elimine el mecanismo responsable (script, tarea programada, malware) y restablezca credenciales si fueron comprometidas.
es.severity_rationale: Es nivel alto porque desactivar un canal de eventos casi nunca es legítimo y deja al SOC sin visibilidad de la actividad posterior.

en.summary: A process wrote DWORD 0 to the Enabled value of a Windows event log channel under WINEVT\Channels. This disables the channel and stops it from recording events.
en.what_it_detects: registry_set events (Sysmon EventID 13) where TargetObject contains \Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WINEVT\Channels\, ends with \Enabled and Details is 'DWORD (0x00000000)'. Excluded: wevtutil.exe, WinSxS TiWorker.exe, TrustedInstaller.exe on Compat-Appraiser, svchost.exe on specific known channels, and events with an empty Image.
en.why_it_matters: An attacker can turn off channels such as Windows Defender/Operational, PowerShell/Operational or Sysmon/Operational to act without leaving a trace. This maps to ATT&CK T1685.001: impairing defenses by disabling Windows event logging.
triage_steps: Identify the channel in TargetObject and how much it matters for security. Defender, PowerShell, Sysmon, Security and TaskScheduler are high priority.
Review the Image, ProcessId and User of the event. Ask whether reg.exe, powershell.exe or an unknown binary has a legitimate reason to change channels.
Find the matching process creation event and inspect the CommandLine and ParentImage chain.
Pivot on the same host within +/- 15 minutes: other WINEVT\Channels changes, wevtutil cl, stopped services or Defender configuration changes.
Check whether the channel is still disabled (wevtutil gl <channel>) and whether events stop after the change time.
Look for earlier alerts for the same user and host, and check for recent remote logons by that user.
Ask IT whether a change ticket or a troubleshooting task explains the change.
false_positives: Administrators disabling a noisy or diagnostic channel during documented troubleshooting.
Installers or configuration management tools that change log channels through the registry rather than wevtutil.
Windows servicing that uses processes the rule's filters do not cover.
response_steps: Confirm with the host owner or the user whether the change was authorized before acting.
If it was not authorized, isolate the endpoint and preserve evidence: a registry export, the remaining logs and the memory of the responsible process.
Re-enable the channel (Enabled = 1 or wevtutil sl <channel> /e:true) and confirm logging resumes.
Investigate activity during the logging gap using EDR, network telemetry and centralized logs.
Remove the responsible mechanism (script, scheduled task, malware) and reset any compromised credentials.
en.severity_rationale: The level is high because disabling an event channel is rarely legitimate and leaves the SOC blind to whatever happens next.

positive.description: reg.exe disables the Windows Defender Operational event channel
PowerShell disables the PowerShell Operational event channel

negative.description: wevtutil.exe sets Enabled to 0 while installing a manifest, which filter_main_wevutil excludes
reg.exe re-enables a channel with DWORD 1, which does not match the Details value
